summary: Edge ingress surge leads to API gateway 5xx spike and upstream runtime watchdog resets
description:
Issue summary: BrightAssist reported a sudden elevation in 5xx errors starting 2026-03-10 02:08 UTC. Errors originate at the API gateway and correlate with repeated upstream runtime watchdog resets and GPU OOMs on a subset of Dedicated pool nodes. Impact: multiple BrightAssist production routes experienced increased latency and ~40% of requests returned 502/503 over a 45-minute window. Environment: prod in us-east-1, tenant pinned to dedicated pool pool-eu-12 (dedicated capacity), model variants pinned to open-rtx-7b-v1.

Observed symptoms: 1) APIGW reported rapid accept-queue growth and SYN backlog spikes. 2) Runtime nodes show repeated watchdog-triggered process restarts with stack traces pointing to prefetch/unmap paths and NVML driver timeouts. 3) Connection churn amplified hedged retry loops from edge causing further load. 4) KV cache thrash seen on serving nodes, heavy mutex contention.

Customer impact: degraded inference success rate for BrightAssist global traffic; customer reported timeouts in their app and opened an escalation ticket to CS.
steps_to_reproduce:
1) Replayed recorded traffic pattern provided by customer (traffic dump id: BA-dump-20260310-0200) at 3x their normal concurrency using local replay harness.
2) Observed accept queue growth on apigw and subsequent 502s when runtime pool evicted processes.
3) Reproduced hedged retry amplification when client retries were set to 2 and network RTTs increased artificially.
4) Enabled debug KV cache logging - observed lock contention and >95% cache eviction rate on warmup windows.

investigation:
Initial hypothesis: edge ingress surge produced accept queue growth which increased request tail latency and led to hedged retries from APIGW. Hedged retries magnified concurrency at serving nodes causing KV cache thrash and GPU memory fragmentation. GPU driver NVML timeouts then triggered runtime watchdog resets. Evidence: timing correlation between apigw accept_queue_ms spikes and runtime watchdog logs; kernel crash counters increased on the same host pool.
Work done:
- Pulled apigw accept queue metrics from 01:50-03:30 UTC and correlated with runtime restart timestamps.
- Scoped affected tenant to pool-eu-12 and isolated nodes exhibiting repeated NVML errors.
- Captured a coredump snapshot from one runtime instance and uploaded to S3 (s3://redwood-dumps/SUP-314200/).
- Temporarily disabled hedged retry policy for BrightAssist route (edge config change id: edge.cfg#20260310-disable-hedge) which reduced retry amplification in a controlled test.
Pending: NVML-level analysis with infra team and test of updated kernel/driver on a canary subset.

resolution: In progress - staged driver update rollout planning. Root cause likely hedged retry amplification combined with NVML driver instability under small-batch high-concurrency leading to GPU timeouts and runtime watchdog resets. Final validation pending canary full production replay for 24h.
workaround: Temporary mitigation applied: hedged retries disabled for affected tenant route and ingress rate-limit lowered for BrightAssist to smooth ramp. This reduced the 5xx rate by ~60% in controlled tests.
final_actions:
1) Complete staged rollout of NV driver 525.95 to affected dedicated pool nodes.
2) Implement an ingress soft-shed policy to limit accept-queue growth for tenant-limited bursts.
3) Adjust default hedged retry thresholds (increase jitter and backoff for retries) and add tenant-aware retry dampening.
4) Add KV cache mutex metrics to alerting and create a runbook for cache-thrashing scenarios.
customer_updates: 2026-03-10 05:00 - Informed customer of immediate mitigations (disabled hedged retries, rate-limit). 2026-03-13 - Shared plan for driver rollout and suggested maintenance windows. Customer requested post-rollout evidence and SLA credit evaluation if errors persist.
notes: This ticket is related to other backpressure/hedged-retry incidents but differs due to NVML/driver-level failures. Recommend de-risking future dedicated pool upgrades by running driver stress tests with small-batch embedding workloads.
